short: The January 2026 memorandum directing an AI-first Department. Seven Pace-Setting Projects, and procurement criteria aimed at model alignment and usage policies.
title: The Department of War AI Strategy
subtitle: Model objectivity and any lawful use as procurement criteria, January 2026
body_html:
On this page

  • The two clauses that reach vendors
  • What the memorandum is
  • The seven Pace-Setting Projects
  • The deadlines
  • How responsible AI is redefined
  • The thread back to the FTC
  • What a vendor should take from this
  • Primary sources

The one-paragraph answer

The Department of War AI Strategy, issued as a memorandum on January 9, 2026, directs the Department to become an “AI-first” warfighting force. Most of it concerns internal acceleration. Two directives reach commercial AI companies: within 90 days the Chief Digital and AI Office is to establish benchmarks for model objectivity as a primary procurement criterion, and within 180 days standard “any lawful use” language is to be written into any Department contract through which AI services are procured. A third makes deploying the latest models within 30 days of public release a procurement criterion too.

The two clauses that reach vendors

Read the memorandum as a supplier and most of it is somebody else’s reorganisation. Two sentences are not.

The first is about how a model behaves. The memorandum states that the Department must not employ AI models which incorporate ideological tuning that interferes with their ability to give objectively truthful responses, and directs the CDAO to establish benchmarks for model objectivity as a primary procurement criterion within 90 days. A benchmark, not a preference. Something a model can be scored against and a contract can turn on.

The second is about what a vendor is allowed to forbid. The memorandum says the Department must utilise models free from usage policy constraints that may limit lawful military applications, and directs that standard “any lawful use” language be incorporated into any Department contract procuring AI services within 180 days.

That second clause is the sharper one. Every major AI provider publishes a usage policy, and those policies are how a company decides what it will not let its model be used for. “Any lawful use” language in a federal contract asks a supplier to set that instrument aside for this customer, within the bounds of law. A company can decline. Declining means declining the contract.

What the memorandum is

It is a direction from the Secretary of War to senior Pentagon leadership, combatant commanders and defense agency directors, dated January 9, 2026. It opens by quoting Executive Order 14179 on sustaining American AI dominance and says the transformation is a race fuelled by commercial AI innovation.

The stated method is to unleash experimentation with leading AI models Department-wide, eliminate bureaucratic barriers to integration, focus investment on American asymmetric advantages including combat-proven operational data from two decades of operations, and run a set of Pace-Setting Projects. It refers to special initiatives in a Classified Annex provided separately, so the public document is not the whole direction.

The seven Pace-Setting Projects

Seven projects are named for fiscal year 2026, each led by a program leader with monthly progress demonstrated to the Deputy Secretary and the Under Secretary for Research and Engineering, and an initial demonstration by a transition-partner user within six months.

  • Warfighting. Swarm Forge, a competitive mechanism to discover and scale ways of fighting with and against AI-enabled capabilities. Agent Network, AI agent development for battle management and decision support, described as reaching from campaign planning to kill chain execution. Ender’s Foundry, AI-enabled simulation.
  • Intelligence. Open Arsenal, accelerating the technical-intelligence-to-capability pipeline, described as turning intel into weapons in hours not years. Project Grant, on deterrence.
  • Enterprise. GenAI.mil, putting AI models directly in the hands of three million civilian and military personnel at all classification levels. Enterprise Agents, a playbook for agent deployment in enterprise workflows.

GenAI.mil is the one with the largest commercial footprint. Three million users at all classification levels is an enterprise deployment on a scale few private customers can match.

The deadlines

From the memoDirection
7 daysA denial of a CDAO data request must be justified to the Under Secretary for Research and Engineering, effective immediately
30 daysEach Military Department, combatant command, defense agency and field activity identifies at least three projects to fast-follow the Pace-Setting Projects; data catalogs delivered to CDAO; each Service Chief and Combatant Commander designates an AI Integration Lead
60 daysEach Component provides AI hiring and talent development plans
90 daysCDAO establishes benchmarks for model objectivity as a primary procurement criterion
180 days“Any lawful use” language incorporated into any Department contract procuring AI services
6 monthsInitial demonstration of each Pace-Setting Project by a transition-partner user

Two further mechanisms are worth naming. The CDAO is directed to act as a “Wartime CDAO”, and the Under Secretary for Research and Engineering is to establish a monthly Barrier Removal Board with authority to waive non-statutory requirements. Program managers acquiring AI capabilities are directed to enforce Modular Open System Architectures, exposing modular interfaces and documentation sufficient for third-party integration without prime contractor support.

How responsible AI is redefined

The memorandum contains a section headed “Clarifying ‘Responsible AI’ at the DoW, Out with Utopian Idealism, In with Hard-Nosed Realism”. It states that diversity, equity and inclusion and social ideology have no place in the Department, and moves from there to the two procurement directives above.

This page reports that because it is the stated reasoning behind a contract term, and a supplier reading only the contract term would not understand where it came from. The site takes no position on the reasoning. What matters operationally is the instruction, and the instruction is specific: benchmarks for model objectivity in 90 days, “any lawful use” in contracts in 180.

The section is also notable for what it does to a phrase. “Responsible AI” has meant, in most federal usage including OMB M-25-21, a set of risk-management practices: testing, impact assessment, monitoring, a fail-safe. Here it is redefined to mean freedom from constraint. Anyone mapping federal AI policy should not assume the term carries the same meaning across documents.

The thread back to the FTC

This is the second federal instrument in twelve months aimed at how AI companies shape model outputs, and the two work from opposite ends.

The FTC’s proposed policy statement on the suppression of accuracy, published July 1, 2026, argues that steering a model toward undisclosed objectives is likely to deceive consumers under Section 5. It reaches the whole market through liability. The Department of War memorandum reaches one customer through procurement, but it is a customer with three million users and a classified annex.

Both trace to Executive Order 14179. Neither creates a rule about model alignment as such. Together they mean a company’s decisions about what its model will and will not do are now visible to a regulator on one side and a contracting officer on the other.

What a vendor should take from this

Four things, in the order they are likely to arrive.

Your usage policy is now a commercial term. If you sell to the Department, expect to be asked to accept “any lawful use”. Decide in advance who in your company can answer that, because the answer is a strategic one rather than a contracting one.

Your release cadence is a criterion. The memorandum directs a delivery and integration cadence enabling the latest models to be deployed within 30 days of public release, and makes it a primary procurement criterion. A vendor whose federal deployment lags its commercial release by a quarter is scored on that.

Your architecture is a criterion. Modular Open System Architectures, with interfaces documented well enough for a third party to integrate without you. That is the opposite of a lock-in strategy, and it is written as a direction to program managers.

Objectivity may become measurable. Benchmarks do not exist yet; they are due 90 days from the memorandum. When they appear, they are the thing to read, because a benchmark is where a contested idea becomes a test a model passes or fails.

Primary sources

The documents behind this summary. Where a decision turns on exact wording, read the source rather than this page.

  • Memorandum for Senior Pentagon Leadership, Commanders of the Combatant Commands, Defense Agency and DoW Field Activity Directors, subject: Artificial Intelligence Strategy for the Department of War, January 9, 2026. Document reference OSD070946-25 / CMD018427-25. A Classified Annex is referenced and provided by separate cover.
  • Executive Order 14179, Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence.
  • Department memorandum “Creating Data Advantage”, May 2021, cited for the federated data catalog requirement.
  • GSA AI Guide for Government, a living reference on organising, workforce, data and AI maturity in federal agencies.
